subject: Connectivity snapshot & performance asks (Redwood private deployment)
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novahealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sasha.patel@novahealth.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connectivity snapshot & performance asks (Redwood private deployment)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation. As promised, here is a short recap of what we need to validate before we can move to procurement for a private (customer-managed) deployment of Redwood in our on-prem datacenter. Please confirm anything that looks off or that you need more detail on.

High-level goals:
- Streaming inference (WebSocket-like session) powering real-time transcription + small-context generative responses for clinical triage UI.
- Target latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms end-to-end (client -> on-prem app -> Redwood inference node -> response back).
- Sustained throughput baseline: 200 requests/sec; burst capacity to 800 req/sec for 10-15s spikes.
- Concurrent streaming sessions: 250 active sessions (each session typically sends small packets ~30 tokens/chunk).
- Egress: traffic will traverse our corporate NAT (10 Gbps pipe) and an AWS Transit Gateway VPN to our cloud VPC for certain services.
- Packet-loss expectation: <0.1%; prefer deterministic RTTs (no >15ms jitter spikes).

Environment specifics (on-prem):
- Firewall outbound via a single NAT IP; outbound TLS to Redwood control/ingress allowed.
- VPN: we plan to pair using AWS TGW (us-west-2) into our on-prem MPLS edge; we can provide transit IP ranges and BGP info.
- Compliance: SOC2 requirement for audit logs and no persistent customer data left on shared hosts; any transfer policies you need to know about.

Immediate asks from Redwood team:
1) A short checklist of network ports/egress destinations and TLS cipher/version expectations.
2) Confirmation you support streaming with session affinity and how you handle prefix caching across failovers.
3) Suggested latency budget breakdown (client->app, app->inference, inference internal processing) so we can reason about where to optimize.
4) A brief outline of the perf test you recommend (tools, sample load profile, expected metrics to capture).

I've attached a sample pcap and a simple topology map to help (nova_network_traces.pcap, nova_topology_map.png).

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering, NovaHealth
alex.nguyen@novahealth.ai | +1 415-555-6187
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novahealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connectivity snapshot & performance asks (Redwood private deployment)

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Threading a quick next-steps plan so we have alignment from our side.

Short answers up front:
- Ports/egress: we need outbound HTTPS (443) to our control plane for model catalog/rollouts and to the inference ingress IPs we provide; streaming uses TLS-over-WebSocket or long-polling depending on deployment (we typically recommend TLS1.3).
- Streaming & affinity: we support session affinity for streaming workloads (sticky routing to a serving node). Prefix/KV caching exists; across failover we replay missing tokens with an automated fall-back that can add ~10-25ms depending on cache warmup.

Questions to clarify your numbers (please confirm):
A) When you say 250 concurrent streaming sessions, is that sustained steady-state, or does it include burst spikes?
B) For the 200 req/sec baseline, is that per-cluster or per-region?
C) Do you expect most sessions to send one chunk every ~300ms, or are they more bursty (e.g., user types then pauses)?

Proposed perf-validation plan (quick):
1) Smoke test: 50 concurrent streaming sessions for 10 minutes (capture p50/p95/p99, packet loss, and egress throughput).
2) Scale test: 250 concurrent streaming sessions for 30 minutes with synthetic burst windows (10s bursts to 800 req/s).
3) Network probe: run continuous ICMP/TCP probes from your edge to our ingress and collect hop-by-hop latency (we'll supply a small agent to run).

I'll attach a short test-plan doc (redwood_test-plan-v1.md) and a link to a minimal checklist (Drive link below). Can you confirm answers to A/B/C above and propose two 2-hour windows next week (preferably US morning) for the smoke and scale tests?

cc: Marissa (solutions), Rishi (runtime eng) — looping you in for test coordination and to capture any SLO hard limits from runtime side.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novahealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sasha.patel@novahealth.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connectivity snapshot & performance asks (Redwood private deployment)

Karthik — quick answers below; Sasha is our infra lead and will run the agents.

A) 250 concurrent sessions should be sustained baseline (we budget for steady-state at that level). Bursts are expected on top of that (spiky traffic during clinic morning start).
B) 200 req/sec baseline is for the local on-prem cluster that will serve the city clinic; we may expand to multi-region later.
C) Session cadence: user typing pattern results in roughly 1 chunk every 250–400ms for active users; we see short idle periods of ~3–8s between multi-turn interactions.

Additional items:
- Egress: all outbound is NATed to single public IP; we will provide the IPs and prefix ACLs.
- VPN: AWS TGW -> on-prem MPLS; we'll provide BGP ASN and the peering window.
- Security: We need confirmation that session logs do not contain PII and that audit logs can be exported to our SIEM.

Attaching nova_network_traces.pcap (2.3MB) and the topology map. Sasha will share preferred test windows shortly.

Alex
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@novahealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Connectivity snapshot & performance asks (Redwood private deployment)

Alex / Sasha — great, thanks for confirming. Quick technical clarifications and an ask to lock windows: 

Clarifications from runtime side (Rishi):
- Cache failover cost: typical extra latency on a cold prefix is ~12–30ms depending on payload size; worst-case an additional ~50ms for full model cold-start but that is rare in our serving profile.
- TCP vs UDP: all inference traffic is TCP/TLS; we rely on TCP reliability for streaming.

Proposed test windows (pick one):
- Option A: Tue 2027-04-27 09:00–11:00 PT (smoke + initial probe)
- Option B: Wed 2027-04-28 09:00–11:00 PT (smoke + scale test run follow-up on Thu)

What we'll deliver after tests:
- Per-hop latency CSV + p50/p95/p99 for request/response times
- Packet loss & jitter graphs, throughput over time, and a short ops-readout deck with recommended mitigations (peering, QoS, or local edge cache).

Action items for NovaHealth before Option A:
1) Share NAT public IPs and allowed egress CIDR list.
2) Provide BGP ASN + TGW peering window details so our network team can pre-configure ACLs.
3) Approve Option A or B.

I'll create the HubSpot task and attach the test plan. Marissa / Rishi — can you confirm availability on Option A?

Thanks,
Karthik
